title: Nut-Free Maple Cinnamon Glaze Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft cinnamon cupcakes soaked in a light maple glaze, then topped with maple frosting, ready in about 43 minutes.
description: These cupcakes start with a soft cinnamon spice base, no nuts anywhere in sight. While they cool, I brush on a thin maple glaze that soaks right into the crumb That glaze step is the trick. It adds a second layer of maple flavor before the frosting even goes on, so every bite tastes deeper than a normal frosted cupcake. I tested this batch for a school bake sale where a few kids have nut allergies, and it disappeared first. The maple frosting on top stays soft, not too sweet, and the cinnamon comes through without being sharp. This is a good fall recipe, but honestly I make it in March too. Maple and cinnamon do not need a season.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, and salt in a bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and 1/3 cup maple syrup.
Alternate adding the flour mix and buttermilk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Whisk 1/4 cup maple syrup, melted butter, and 1/4 tsp cinnamon for the glaze. Brush over warm cupcake tops and let soak in 10 minutes.
Beat 1 cup butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar, 3 tbsp maple syrup, and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. Beat until fluffy.
Pipe or spread frosting on fully cooled, glazed cupcakes. Dust with extra cinnamon if you like.
tips: Brush the glaze on while the cupcakes are still warm so it soaks into the crumb instead of sitting on top.
Use real maple syrup, not pancake syrup. It makes a real flavor difference here.
If your kitchen is warm, chill the frosting 10 minutes before piping so it holds its shape.
Double check labels on syrup and butter brands if baking for someone with a nut allergy, since cross contact can happen in shared facilities.

faq.question: Why glaze the cupcakes before frosting them?
faq.answer: The glaze soaks into the warm cake and adds maple flavor inside the crumb. Frosting alone only sits on top, so the glaze gives you a second layer of taste in every bite.

faq.question: Can I make this recipe ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes. Bake and glaze the cupcakes up to a day ahead, then store them covered at room temperature. Add the frosting the day you plan to serve them.

faq.question: Is this recipe safe for a nut allergy bake sale?
faq.answer: The recipe itself uses no nuts or nut extracts. Check that your specific brands of butter, flour, and syrup are processed in a nut-free facility if allergies are severe.

faq.question: Can I skip the glaze step to save time?
faq.answer: You can, but you will lose the layered maple flavor that makes this recipe different from a plain spice cupcake. The glaze only takes a few extra minutes.

conclusion: These cupcakes give you two layers of maple flavor in one bite, and they are simple enough for a weeknight bake. Try the glaze trick once and you will use it on other cupcakes too.
